Mr. Edward Peabody, PreJident of .Masonic Home of California:
Dl:AR Sra AND BROTHER-I submit this report of. my examination of
the accounts of the MASONIC HOME OF CALIFORNIA.
I with great care and detail, verified· the tabulated account of
monthly payments, showing an expenditure of $33,449 09 and also the
lengthy itemized schedule of the various payments from September 1st,
1906, to August 31st, 1907 inclusive, and pleasurably testify to the
absolute accuracy therof.
Also, as per previous report, I similarly verified the Special Christmas. Gift account, 1906, with' receipts and disbursements alike of $2,203.
Other items I was unable to pass upon, for the reason that I was
not furri!shed with the necessary pass-books and vouchers, but reasonably conclude they a re also correct.
Respectfully,
Taos. T . ATKINSON, C. P. A .

In conclusion, it is with pleasure for me to add that the books of
the Secretary are a model of neatness, that all accounts of both Officers
are entirely correct, and the results must prove gratifying to the members of this M,.". W.". Grand Lodge, and to all interested brethren.
Very respectfully;
Tnos. T. ATKINSON, Certified Public Accountant.

shall be for the payment of Representatives, and shall be · paid at the
same time and in the manner prescribed for the payment of the
annual dues.

Bro. Thomas J. Baker presented the following report:
To the M:. w:. Grand Lodge of California :
Your Committee to whom was referred the report of the Very ·
w: · William Harvey Edwards, Grand Lecturer, beg to report as
follows:
The Grand Lodge, the Inspectors and the Officers of the various
Lodges of this Grand jurisdiction have sustained a severe loss in the
retirement of Bro. Edwards as Grand Lecturer-<me who has been so
patient and painstaking in teaching the work to the brethren, yet
insiiting upon letter perfect work-always commending where it was
*For items see pages 668-675.

due, and never failing 'to censure where necessary, both Inspectors and
Officers ; yet done in that firm but pleasant way that could offend none.
We all love Bro. Edwards for his true worth as a man and a Mason
and the Grand Lodge and Masonry in general is to be congratulated
for having held for so many "years so efficient a Grand Officer and
teacher-one who was so peculiarly fitted for the position.
. We are pleased to note' from Bro. Edwards' report that he has
found the work done in most of the Lodges in a most creditable
manner, and that also in the Lodges that are so remotely situated as to
make it impossible.for the officers to obtain the necessary instruction.
yet the same spirit prevails for good work. . Such a report, coming as it
does from our Grand Lecturer, bespeaks much as a reward for his
patient and tireless teaching. 'While we are to lose Bro. Edwards as
our instructor, we are pleased to know that he has been placed in a
higher post of trust-one to which he is eminently fitted to fill not only
with great credit to ~imself, but with honor to our noble Fraternity.
And in conclusion we feel ' that we voice the sentiment of every
Mason in this jurisdiction when we .wish Bro. Edwards success and
God's richest blessiqg.
Respectfully submitted,
JAM ES

Constitution and General Regulations
Adopted Oct. A. L. 5907.

JOHN SAMUEL .JOHNSON, P. M.
Oxnard Lodg·~, No. 341.·.•......•...• Died March 25, 1907

That Section.. 11, of Article III, Part III, of the Constitution be
and is hereby amended to read as follows :

ADOLPH COHN, P. M.
Starr King Lodge, No. 344 ........ Died December 8, 1906

f

Sec. 11. No Lodge shall expel a member for the non-payment of
dues ; but, in case any member shall have refused or neglected to pay
his regular dues during a period of twelve months he shall be notified
by the Secretary, either by registered letter or by actual service of
notice, duly certified by the Tyler, that unless at the next stated
meeting either his dues be paid or sickness or inability to pay be shown
as the cause of such· refusal or neglect, he will be suspended from all
the rights and privileges of Masonry. If neither of these things be
.done, he shall at such stated meeting be declared by the Master to be
suspended, unless for special reasons shown the Lodge shall remit his
dues or grant him further time for their payment: But any Mason
thus suspended who shall at any time pay the arrearages due at the
time of his suspension, together with such further dues as would, had
he retained his membership, have accrued against him to the date of
such payment, or who shall have had such arrearages and dues remitted
by his Lodge, shall by either of these acts be restored; Provided, that
-should any member suspended for non-payment of dues neglect for the
-period of two years to pay dues or have the same remitted by his
Lodge, said member shall not be restored except by a three-fourths
vote by ballot of all the members present at the next stated meeting
.after the petition for restoration is presented.
Any Secretary failing or neglecting to comply with the requirements
of this section relative to notifying delinquents shall be subject to
·discipline by his Lodge for neglect of duty.
The term "Past Master," as defined in Article II of Part VII of
the Constitution, is hereby amended and modified to read as follows :
This title applies only to one who has been regularly elected or
named in a charter and installed and has served a term as Master of
a chartered Lodge within the jurisdiction of this Grand Lodge and

748

. GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA.

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

749

who remains a member in good standing of one of its subordinates;
provided, that one who has been regularly elected or named in a charter and installed and has served a term as Master of a chartered Lodge
within the jurisdiction of any other Grand Lodge recognized by this
Grand Lodge, and who has affiliated with or become a member of a
subordinate Lodge within this jurisdiction and who remains a member
in good standing of one of its subordinates may take the honorary title
of "Past Master," but shall not thereby become a member of this Grand
Lodge.

EXPULSIONS AND SUSPENSIONS
GENERAL REGULATION No. 2, REPEALED.
EXPULSIONS BY LODGES AFFIRMED:

That General Regulation No. 21 is hereby repealed, and that the
following be and is hereby adopted in place of it:
Regulation 21. All Lodges in this Jurisdiction are authorized to
employ, in the conduct of Masonic trials, a duly accredited stenographic
reporter; Provided, That said stenographic reporter is a Master Mason
and that, before entering upon his duty he shall be qualified in the manner provided for the qualification of Masonic witnesses; and provided
further, that said stenographic reporter shall attest the transcript of 'the
evidence of the respective witnesses examined in the course of the trial
prior to signature by the said witnesses; and, provided further, that the
employment of a stenographic reporter in any such trials shall be
optional with the Master presiding at said trial.
